problem:
The equation below describes all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(0,-2,2)$ and $Q(1,-1,1).$

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ a\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ b \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,t\in [c,1]
$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Line

feedback.problem:
The equation below gives a parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(4,3,5)$ and $Q(6,3,1).$

$$
r(t)=(2t+4)\,i+a\,j+b\,k,\,t\in [0,c]
$$

What is $a+b+c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(6\,i+3\,j+k)-(4\,i+3\,j+5\,k) \\  & =2\,i-4\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
r=p+tv\,⟹\,r=(4\,i+3\,j+5\,k)+t(2\,i-4\,k)
$$

and the parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(4\,i+3\,j+5\,k)+t(2\,i-4\,k) \\  & =(2t+4)\,i+3\,j+(5-4t)\,k,\,t\in [0,1].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=3+(5-4t)+1=9-4t.
$$
